justifications.functional_suitability: All functional requirements are comprehensively addressed by dedicated elements: Consultation Management and Media Relay & Signaling Service for consultations, Prescription Router Component for e-prescriptions, Inference Controller for AI triage, and Consent Ledger for consent management.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance targets are met using Memorystore Redis for distributed rate limiting and caching, an Asyncio Queue in Audit & Traceability Logger to avoid blocking inference, and Bandwidth Adaptation Monitor for real-time video stream optimization.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is thoroughly covered by US HL7 FHIR Adapter Component, EU National Gateway Adapter Component, and secure mTLS gateways for national prescription networks, alongside WebRTC integration via SFU Media Router to Third-party Video Infrastructure.
justifications.usability: Patients and Licensed Clinicians are provided multi-channel access through Web Portal Interface and Mobile App Client with offline-first client caching. However, specific usability mechanisms for clinicians' specialized workflows or degraded-network UX feedback are not fully detailed.
justifications.reliability: Reliability under poor network conditions is achieved via Bandwidth Adaptation Monitor adjusting Simulcast/SVC layers and TURN/STUN Relay Module. In addition, Idempotency Store Component prevents duplicate prescription requests, and Rate Limiting & Degradation Handler manages network degradation.
justifications.security: Security and compliance are thoroughly enforced: Geo-Routing & Region Enforcer and regional Cloud SQL PostgreSQL guarantee data residency; Cloud KMS provides envelope encryption; Authentication & Consent Verifier enforces permissions; and Audit & Traceability Logger ensures EU MDR compliance.
justifications.maintainability: The system shows high modularity with decoupled containers and explicit component boundaries, such as separating regional adapters in US HL7 FHIR Adapter Component and EU National Gateway Adapter Component, and isolating AI logic in AI Symptom Checker Orchestrator.
justifications.portability: The system targets GCP regions (europe-west3, us-central1) using containerized Go, Python, and Node.js services alongside Web Portal Interface and Mobile App Client (Flutter). It relies moderately on GCP-specific managed services like Memorystore and Cloud SQL PostgreSQL.

PERF-01.justification: Media Relay uses SFU/LiveKit with WebRTC offloading to handle high-concurrency video routing, and Redis Pub/Sub provides low-latency signaling coordination.
sensitivity_points: Signaling throughput in Redis Pub/Sub during connection establishment spikes
SFU media routing capacity under concurrent session negotiation
tradeoffs: Offloading media relay to third-party WebRTC reduces server compute but increases vendor dependence

PERF-02.justification: Handling ~14 requests/sec is lightweight for FastAPI and gRPC; asynchronous queueing decouples audit logging from the sub-3s synchronous response path.
sensitivity_points: Latency of the external AI Symptom Checker Service inference endpoint
Asynchronous queue capacity before audit log writes to Cloud SQL
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit logging improves response times but risks transient data loss if instances crash

AVAIL-01.justification: Bandwidth Adaptation Monitor actively tracks packet metrics and dynamically switches Simulcast/SVC layers to maintain streams at degraded bitrates below 300 kbit/s.
sensitivity_points: Speed of detecting network degradation and throttling SVC video layers
Audio stream prioritization over video during severe bandwidth throttling
tradeoffs: Aggressive video quality degradation preserves call continuity at the expense of visual fidelity

AVAIL-02.justification: Only us-central1 is configured for the US; no secondary US region or automated regional failover mechanisms exist to restore US service without EU residency violations.
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary regional infrastructure in the US cloud boundary
Data residency constraints prohibiting disaster recovery routing into europe-west3
tradeoffs: Restricting US data strictly to us-central1 prevents cross-region DR failover without a second US region

MOD-01.justification: Prescription Router dispatches normalized internal payloads to dedicated regional adapter components, isolating new national standards to an added adapter.
sensitivity_points: Expressiveness of the normalized internal prescription schema across diverse national standards
Decoupling of national transport protocols from core dispatching logic
tradeoffs: Canonical prescription data models introduce mapping overhead but isolate country-specific adapter logic

MOD-02.justification: The orchestrator and Audit & Traceability Logger explicitly capture model versions and inference inputs into append-only audit schemas, ensuring verifiable lineage.
sensitivity_points: Explicit model version propagation in external AI inference requests and responses
Immutability guarantees within the Cloud SQL audit logging schema
tradeoffs: Comprehensive audit logging per inference increases database storage requirements for traceability compliance

SEC-01.justification: Geo-Routing enforces regional perimeters while Authentication & Consent Verifier and Consent Ledger intercept cross-region requests and enforce explicit patient consent before logging.
sensitivity_points: Fast policy verification using Redis-backed consent state at the API edge
Tamper-proof audit logging of cross-border clinician access attempts
tradeoffs: Strict consent verification at gateway layers introduces slight request latency to guarantee compliance

SEC-02.justification: Consent Ledger updates patient preferences and invalidates cache states immediately, and Audit & Traceability logs the revocation for compliance verification.
sensitivity_points: Cache invalidation latency across distributed Redis session and policy stores
Verification workflows confirming complete downstream cessation of research data pipelines
tradeoffs: Immediate cache invalidation creates downstream cache misses but ensures rapid consent enforcement
